papers.title: Predicting Rheumatoid Arthritis Flares Using Wearable Device Data: Deep Learning Study.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares are common and unpredictable. Current monitoring relies on episodic clinical visits and laboratory testing, thereby limiting the ability to anticipate disease worsening. Wearable devices may support continuous remote monitoring, but models must account for missing real-world data, heterogeneous consumer devices, and the distinction between symptomatic disease activity and systemic inflammation.
papers.summary: This study develops deep learning models that use wearable device data to predict flares in rheumatoid arthritis patients, addressing real-world challenges like missing data and heterogeneous consumer devices. It distinguishes between symptomatic disease activity and systemic inflammation, aiming to enable continuous remote monitoring beyond episodic clinical visits. The work demonstrates the potential of wearables for anticipatory flare prediction in chronic disease management.

papers.title: Biophysically grounded deep learning improves protein-protein ΔΔG prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding free energy (ΔΔG) remains limited by small, redundant datasets and train-test homology leakage. We show that commonly used SKEMPI2 splits inflate model performance, with every tested AI predictor declining under a stringent split that controls homology at the level of individual chains (60% sequence identity). We introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that integrates five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations through cross-embedding attention. Under leakage-controlled evaluation,
papers.summary: The authors show that standard SKEMPI2 train-test splits leak homology and inflate the apparent accuracy of AI predictors of mutation-induced protein-protein binding free energy changes (ΔΔG). They introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that fuses five residue-level biophysical descriptors with pretrained protein embeddings via cross-embedding attention, and demonstrate improved performance under a stringent homology-controlled split (60% chain identity).

papers.title: Protein sequence domain annotation using a language model.
papers.abstract: Protein domain annotation underlies large-scale functional inference and is commonly performed by scanning sequences against libraries of profile hidden Markov models (profile HMMs). We describe PSALM, a protein domain annotation method that combines (i) a pretrained protein language model (ESM-2) with (ii) a per-residue domain-state classifier and (iii) a structured probabilistic decoder that produces a single, non-overlapping set of domain calls with explicit boundaries and scores. On a benchmark of 76.9M protein sequences with 107M annotated domains, PSALM attains a domain-detection sensiti
papers.summary: PSALM is a new method for annotating protein domains that combines a pretrained protein language model (ESM-2) with a per-residue domain-state classifier and a structured probabilistic decoder to produce non-overlapping domain calls with explicit boundaries and scores. Benchmarked on 76.9M protein sequences with 107M annotated domains, it improves domain-detection sensitivity over traditional profile HMM scanning. This offers a language-model-based alternative to the standard HMM-based annotation pipeline.

papers.title: MissenseDB: proteome-wide human missense variant effect prediction database with structural context.
papers.abstract: Missense variant-effect predictors now provide proteome-scale estimates of amino acid substitution impact, but their outputs remain distributed across independent resources and are difficult to explore jointly with protein structural and human-variation context. We present MissenseDB, a residue-centric database integrating three architecturally distinct transformer-based predictors, AlphaMissense, VESM-3B, and VESPA, across the reviewed human proteome. MissenseDB contains 10 734 339 residue positions across 19 436 canonical human proteins, with complete three-predictor coverage for 19 434 prot
papers.summary: MissenseDB is a new database that integrates predictions from three transformer-based missense variant effect predictors (AlphaMissense, VESM-3B, and VESPA) across the reviewed human proteome, covering over 10.7 million residue positions in 19,436 canonical proteins. It provides residue-centric, proteome-wide variant effect estimates alongside protein structural and human variation context, making it easier to jointly explore predictions that were previously scattered across separate resources.

papers.title: ARCADE: Controllable Codon Design from Foundation Models via Activation Engineering.
papers.abstract: Coding sequence design requires optimizing multiple biological properties, which may be either aligned or in trade-off, and are typically measured as continuous-valued metrics. However, existing codon design methods lack explicit control over these objectives. Moreover, current controllable generation techniques are largely developed for discrete, human-interpretable attributes, leaving a gap in controllably steering continuous biological properties in genomic sequence design.
papers.summary: ARCADE introduces a method for controllable codon design by applying activation engineering to protein foundation models, enabling steering of continuous biological properties (e.g., expression, folding) in generated coding sequences. This addresses a gap where existing controllable generation techniques target discrete, human-interpretable attributes rather than continuous genomic design objectives. The approach allows optimization of multiple, potentially trade-off, properties without retraining.

papers.title: Ecological Context in Computational Discovery of Microbiome-Derived Antimicrobial Peptides.
papers.abstract: Computational mining of microbiomes has expanded antimicrobial peptide (AMP) discovery from individual organisms to millions of predicted sequences. The challenge is now to identify candidates that merit experimental investigation and to determine what their validation reveals about biological function. Ecological information may describe sequence provenance, support interpretation after prediction, guide candidate prioritization or contribute directly to model development. These uses are distinct, and the presence of ecological metadata does not by itself show that context improved discovery.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that while computational mining of microbiome data has generated millions of predicted antimicrobial peptide sequences, ecological context is often invoked without demonstrating that it actually improves discovery. The authors distinguish several distinct uses of ecological metadata—describing sequence provenance, aiding post-prediction interpretation, prioritizing candidates, or informing model development—and caution that the mere presence of such metadata does not prove its utility. The paper calls for clearer evaluation of whether ecological context genuinely enhances AMP discovery pipelines.

papers.title: LiteMicroFormer: A Lightweight Attention-Guided Transformer with Adaptive Cluster Under-Sampling for Metagenomic Disease Prediction.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional microbial abundance profiles, limited sample sizes, and severe class imbalance make accurate disease prediction from human gut metagenomics challenging. To address these limitations, we propose LiteMicroFormer, a lightweight attention-guided transformer framework for disease-specific binary classification using species-level microbiome profiles and metadata. LiteMicroFormer embeds species values, applies feature-gating attention, extracts microbial representations through a transformer, fuses metadata, and uses attention pooling to capture informative low-complexity patterns.
papers.summary: LiteMicroFormer is a lightweight transformer framework for predicting disease status from gut metagenomic species-abundance profiles, designed to cope with high dimensionality, small sample sizes, and class imbalance. It combines feature-gating attention, metadata fusion, attention pooling, and adaptive cluster under-sampling to capture informative patterns from low-complexity microbiome data.

papers.title: Comparative Accuracy of a Commercial Multimodal Large Language Model Versus Clinicians in Dental Age and Sex Estimation from Panoramic Radiographs: A Benchmark Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Routine dental imaging captures cumulative dentoalveolar and periodontal changes, offering a non-invasive window into both chronological aging and physiological senescence. While task-specific deep learning models have been widely explored in dental radiology, the zero-shot diagnostic performance of commercial Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in adult populations remains underinvestigated. The aim of this study was to benchmark the zero-shot diagnostic accuracy and repeatability of a commercial MLLM against human clinicians of varying experience levels in estimat
papers.summary: This benchmark study compared a commercial multimodal large language model against clinicians of varying experience levels for estimating dental age and sex from panoramic radiographs in adults. The MLLM was evaluated in a zero-shot setting, without task-specific training, to assess its diagnostic accuracy and repeatability relative to human experts. The findings provide an early indication of how off-the-shelf multimodal models perform on specialized dental imaging tasks compared with trained clinicians.

papers.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.
papers.summary: This paper expands the known clinical spectrum of TUBGCP6-related primary microcephaly, reporting patients with severe cortical malformations but without the chorioretinopathy typically associated with the condition. It also provides insights into how TUBGCP6 variants should be interpreted, noting that most previously reported cases carried at least one loss-of-function variant.

papers.title: Enhanced prognosis stratification following surgery for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma to optimize clinical decisions by reflecting tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has an extremely dismal postoperative prognosis. Conventional TNM staging cannot adequately characterize tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment, leading to suboptimal risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an integrated prognostic system for PDAC by combining deep learning (DL)-based radiomic features with guideline‑recommended clinicopathological variables.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates an integrated prognostic system for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that combines deep learning-based radiomic features with standard clinicopathological variables to better stratify postoperative risk. The approach aims to capture tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment information that conventional TNM staging misses, potentially improving clinical decision-making after surgery.

papers.title: Machine learning and the protein corona: importance of nanoparticle, protein, and experimental features.
papers.abstract: Nanoparticles (NPs) present in any biological environment are rapidly coated with a "corona" of proteins on the surface of the NPs. This protein corona, rather than the bare NP, determines the biological response to the protein-NP complex. The use of machine learning to predict which proteins will adsorb on the surface of a NP would accelerate the development of new NPs. We provide a detailed examination of two random forest models, random forest regression (RFR) and classification (RFC), to determine how corona prediction is impacted by the biophysics, data structure, and statistics of the sy
papers.summary: This study examines how random forest regression and classification models predict which proteins adsorb onto nanoparticle surfaces to form the protein corona, a layer that determines biological responses to nanoparticles. The authors analyze how nanoparticle properties, protein biophysics, and experimental data structure affect prediction performance, providing guidance on feature selection for corona prediction models. The work aims to accelerate nanoparticle development by improving machine learning approaches to predict protein-nanoparticle interactions.

papers.title: Integrated Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analyses Highlight IAPP as a Molecular Feature Associated with β-Cell Identity Remodeling in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
papers.abstract: β-cell identity remodeling is an important feature of β-cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but its associated molecular characteristics remain incompletely understood. This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, machine learning, protein-protein interaction network analysis, gene set variation analysis, and computational perturbation to characterize β-cell identity-associated molecular features. IAPP emerged as the sole overlapping candidate from the integrated machine-learning and PPI analyses and was reduced in T2DM islets. Its expression was positively corr
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data with machine learning and network analyses to identify molecular features of β-cell identity remodeling in type 2 diabetes. IAPP emerged as the top candidate gene, showing reduced expression in T2DM islets and correlating with β-cell identity markers. The findings position IAPP as a potential molecular feature linked to β-cell dysfunction in T2DM.

papers.title: Automated Chest Diseases Classification Using Multimodal Deep Learning.
papers.abstract: Computer-Aided Diagnosis systems can support physicians by reducing workload, medical errors, and time required for patient care. However, many existing systems primarily rely on medical images while overlooking valuable information available in associated medical reports. This study proposes a multimodal deep learning approach for chest disease classification by integrating chest X-ray images and radiology reports from the MIMIC-CXR dataset. (2) Methods: Different Deep Learning models are evaluated for each modality, followed by a comprehensive comparison of intermediate and late fusion strat
papers.summary: This study develops a multimodal deep learning system that combines chest X-ray images with their associated radiology reports to classify chest diseases, using the MIMIC-CXR dataset. The authors compare several deep learning architectures per modality and evaluate intermediate versus late fusion strategies for integrating the two data sources. The work shows that incorporating textual report information alongside imaging can improve automated diagnosis compared with image-only approaches.

papers.title: Fungal laccases: a double-edged sword linking environmental adaptation and pathogenicity.
papers.abstract: Laccases (EC 1.10.3.2) are multicopper oxidases that oxidize diverse phenolic and non-phenolic compounds while reducing oxygen to water. Despite their highly conserved catalytic architectures, fungal laccases perform diverse biological functions depending on ecological context. In saprophytic fungi, they contribute to lignin degradation, nutrient acquisition, carbon cycling, and pollutant detoxification, supporting their application in bioremediation, wastewater treatment, biofuel production, and green chemistry. In certain pathogenic fungi, laccases contribute to lineage-specific processes as
papers.summary: This review examines fungal laccases, a family of copper-containing enzymes that oxidize a wide range of phenolic and non-phenolic compounds. In saprophytic fungi, laccases support lignin breakdown, nutrient acquisition, and pollutant detoxification, making them useful for bioremediation and biofuel production. In pathogenic fungi, the same enzymes contribute to lineage-specific processes tied to infection, illustrating how a conserved enzyme family can serve both environmental adaptation and virulence.

papers.title: Reading the Host from the Virus: A Systematic Review of Sequence-Based Prediction of Host-Related Properties for Eukaryote-Infecting Viruses.
papers.abstract: Viral metagenomics and metatranscriptomics have expanded our understanding of viral diversity and associations between viruses and hosts. For eukaryotic viruses, identifying host-related properties remains challenging because infection depends on receptor compatibility, tissue specificity and mechanisms of immune evasion. Interspecies transmission and zoonotic spillover pose major risks to global health, highlighting the need for computational methods that can prioritise plausible host associations and related risks for known and novel viruses. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematical
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys computational methods that predict host-related properties of eukaryote-infecting viruses directly from viral sequence data, covering host range, tropism, and zoonotic risk. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, it catalogues and compares the available sequence-based prediction approaches, highlighting their utility for prioritizing host associations of known and novel viruses in metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies. The review provides a structured overview of the field's methods and gaps for researchers working on viral host prediction and spillover risk assessment.

papers.title: Integrating Inflammatory and Endothelial Biomarkers in Machine Learning Models to Predict Sepsis Development in Critically Ill Patients: A Combined Retrospective and Prospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Sepsis is a severe, life-threatening condition in which timely recognition improves patient outcomes. Machine learning (ML) methods, usually relying on vital sign data, have shown promise in early sepsis prediction; however, they underrepresent sepsis biomarkers, which are widely used in clinical practice. We aimed to develop and validate interpretable ML models for early sepsis prediction using non-temporal data from the first 24 h of intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and to quantify the incremental value of inflammatory (Interleukin-6 (IL-6), procalcitonin (PCT), C-Reactive Protein (CRP))
papers.summary: This multicenter study developed and validated interpretable machine learning models for early sepsis prediction in ICU patients using non-temporal data from the first 24 hours of admission, incorporating inflammatory biomarkers (IL-6, PCT, CRP) alongside endothelial markers. The authors quantified the incremental predictive value of adding these biomarkers to standard vital-sign-based models, addressing a gap where clinical biomarkers are underrepresented in ML sepsis prediction tools.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Abiotic Stress-Responsive Genes in Date Palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.).
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses pose major constraints to Phoenix dactylifera L. productivity in different environments. Although date palm possesses substantial adaptive capacity, experimentally validated stress-responsive gene resources remain limited. Here, we developed a sequence-based machine learning framework to prioritize candidate abiotic stress-responsive genes in date palm. Training labels were derived computationally: the 48,801-protein reference proteome was annotated by best-hit orthology to Arabidopsis thaliana, and stress-associated Gene Ontology terms transferred from these orthologs were us
papers.summary: The authors built a sequence-based machine learning framework to prioritize candidate abiotic stress-responsive genes in date palm, using stress-associated Gene Ontology terms transferred from Arabidopsis orthologs as training labels. This provides a computational resource for identifying stress-response candidates in a crop with limited experimentally validated gene annotations.

papers.title: Predicting Pediatric Appendicitis: A Comparative Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Routine Laboratory Parameters.
papers.abstract: Background: Routine laboratory blood tests are central in evaluating children with suspected appendicitis. Machine learning (ML) offers promise for improving diagnostic accuracies by predicting from variables that are non-linearly associated. We explored and internally validated ML models in their prediction of appendicitis with routine laboratory parameters in comparison with logistic regression and established clinical algorithms. Methods: We carried out a secondary analysis of a public dataset of 780 children admitted with suspected appendicitis of which 463 (59.4%) were diagnosed with appe
papers.summary: This study compared machine learning models against logistic regression and established clinical scoring systems for predicting pediatric appendicitis using routine laboratory blood tests in a public dataset of 780 children. The authors used explainable ML methods to identify which lab parameters drive predictions, aiming to improve diagnostic accuracy over conventional approaches. The work is a secondary analysis with internal validation only, so findings require external confirmation before clinical use.

papers.title: Quercetin Alleviates PFOS-Induced Inflammatory Responses in Human Microvascular Endothelial Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: Perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) is a ubiquitous industrial chemical linked to cardiovascular toxicity. Quercetin, a plant-derived flavonoid, exhibits known anti-inflammatory properties. While PFOS induces endothelial dysfunctions, the molecular mechanisms underlying quercetin's protective effects remain unclear. Methods: We integrated transcriptomic analysis and in vitro experiments to investigate these mechanisms in human microvascular endothelial cells (HMEC-1). Results: Five overlapping hub genes between PFOS and quercetin targets (IL6, RELA, VEGFA, CXCL8 and PIM1) were ide
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic analysis with in vitro experiments to show that the flavonoid quercetin counteracts PFOS-induced inflammatory responses in human microvascular endothelial cells. Five hub genes (IL6, RELA, VEGFA, CXCL8, and PIM1) were identified as overlapping targets of PFOS and quercetin, suggesting these as key mediators of the protective effect.

papers.title: Treatment Selection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Conceptual Framework for Precision Therapy.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a major therapeutic challenge, with limited improvement in outcomes and substantial heterogeneity in treatment response. Systemic chemotherapy remains a cornerstone of treatment across disease stages, yet treatment selection, particularly in metastatic PDAC (mPDAC), is still driven predominantly by clinical characteristics, performance status, prior therapy, and a limited number of molecular biomarkers. The emergence of biomarker-directed therapies, including strategies targeting oncogenic KRAS alterations, demonstrates the potential of molecular
papers.summary: This review proposes a conceptual framework for precision therapy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), arguing that treatment selection should move beyond clinical characteristics toward biomarker-directed strategies. It highlights emerging molecularly targeted approaches, such as those targeting oncogenic KRAS alterations, as evidence that molecular profiling can guide therapy in this heterogeneous disease.

papers.title: Combining Machine Learning Approaches and In Vitro Assays to Identify Novel ACE- and DPP-IV-Inhibitory Peptides from Complex Duckweed (Lemnoideae) Protein Hydrolysates.
papers.abstract: Identifying peptide sequences responsible for the bioactivity of complex food protein hydrolysates remains a challenge in the development of functional food ingredients, especially from novel protein sources such as duckweed (Lemnoideae) hydrolysates. A dataset comprising 407 peptides, their features as well as the ACE and DPP-IV inhibitory activities of the different global fractions was constructed, and four complementary statistical and machine learning approaches, Random Forest regression, Partial Least Squares regression, Linear Regression, and Pearson correlation, were applied to associa
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning models (Random Forest, PLS, linear regression, and correlation analysis) with in vitro assays to identify peptide sequences responsible for ACE and DPP-IV inhibitory activity in complex duckweed protein hydrolysates. Using a dataset of 407 peptides, the authors link peptide features to bioactivity of global fractions, demonstrating an approach to deconvolute functional peptides from novel plant protein sources. The work supports the development of duckweed as a sustainable source of bioactive food ingredients.

papers.title: Cross-Disease Integration Identifies Inflammation-Related Candidate Biomarkers for Atherosclerosis and Candidate Therapeutic Compounds Using Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a translational research framework integrating cross-disease computational screening with experimental validation. Using Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection as a cross-disease inflammatory comparator, we systematically identified atherosclerosis-associated hub genes through integrated bioinformatics and machine-learning analyses, evaluated their potential diagnostic value in independent datasets, and validated their protein expression in a mouse model of atherosclerosis (AS). Methods: GEO gene-expression datasets were analyzed using differential e
papers.summary: This study built a computational pipeline combining differential expression analysis, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify inflammation-related hub genes shared between H. pylori infection and atherosclerosis, then validated candidate protein expression in a mouse atherosclerosis model. The work nominates candidate diagnostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic compounds for atherosclerosis, using an infection as a cross-disease inflammatory comparator.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto
papers.summary: This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammation. The authors integrate cheminformatics and machine learning approaches to identify and prioritize potential TLR-targeted therapeutic compounds. The work is a synthesis of immunopathogenesis with computational drug-discovery strategies rather than new experimental data.

papers.title: LGALS1-Associated Candidate Myeloid Signature and In Silico Regulatory Analysis in Ulcerative Colitis: A Bioinformatics Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Ulcerative colitis (UC) substantially impairs patients' quality of life and increases the risk of colorectal carcinogenesis. However, its precise molecular pathogenesis remains to be elucidated. Methods: Bioinformatic tools and methods were used to achieve the objectives of this study. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, genome-wide association study (GWAS), and single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL) data to comprehensively identify key molecular determinants underlying UC. scPagwas and Scissor analyses were performed to iden
papers.summary: This bioinformatics study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, bulk transcriptome, GWAS, and sc-eQTL data to identify a LGALS1-associated myeloid cell signature in ulcerative colitis. The authors use pathway-based and phenotype-scoring tools (scPagwas, Scissor) to link genetic risk variants to specific cell states and propose candidate regulatory mechanisms. The work is exploratory and in silico, so the findings require experimental validation.

papers.title: Proteomics Reveals Stress-Related Proteins in the Embryonic Axis of Chickpea Sprouts Grown Under Green and Red LED Light.
papers.abstract: Stress-related proteins are overexpressed in plants under adverse growth conditions, helping them to survive. The identification and quantification of these proteins are limited in non-model organisms. Furthermore, the high concentration of storage proteins commonly found in seeds increases the difficulty of studying them. Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) is one of the most consumed legumes worldwide. Nevertheless, the proteins implicated in stress response have not been explored sufficiently in this organism. Light-emitting diode (LED) light has been used to improve crop quality for a long time;
papers.summary: This study used proteomics to identify stress-related proteins in the embryonic axis of chickpea sprouts grown under green and red LED light. The work addresses the challenge of studying low-abundance stress proteins in non-model plants where storage proteins dominate the seed proteome. It provides a catalog of light-responsive stress proteins in a major legume crop.

papers.title: Dual-Magnification Deep Learning Predicts KRASG12D Status from H&E Images of Pancreatic Cancer: A Multi-Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Background: KRAS mutations occur in over 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAC), and KRASG12D is the most frequent variant. G12D-selective inhibitors are now in clinical development, but computational pathology has so far predicted mutation status only at the gene level, leaving allele-specific prediction unexplored. Because genomic testing can be time-consuming and costly, a tool that predicts KRASG12D mutation status from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images could help identify patients for confirmatory molecular testing and potential treatment with KRASG12D inhibitors. Here w
papers.summary: This study develops a dual-magnification deep learning model that predicts KRASG12D allele-specific mutation status directly from routine H&E-stained pancreatic cancer images, validated across multiple patient cohorts. It moves beyond gene-level KRAS prediction to variant-level inference, potentially enabling rapid triage of patients for confirmatory molecular testing and G12D-selective inhibitor eligibility.

papers.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important cha
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces st2sc, a computational method for recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses the challenge that each spatial spot aggregates signals from multiple cells by explicitly identifying individual cells and estimating per-gene expression, improving on existing methods that struggle with accurate gene-level estimation.

papers.title: Target-Specific Benchmarking of Potency Prediction on Activity-Cliff Compounds Across 33 Human Protein Targets Using Inhibition Constants.
papers.abstract: Activity cliffs are pairs of closely related compounds whose potencies differ far more than their structures suggest, and the compounds involved in them remain a leading cause of local failure in ligand-based potency prediction. The MoleculeACE benchmark established that models predict these compounds poorly and that the gap differs between datasets. What has been missing is a panel built on one activity endpoint, a per-target account of how large the gap is, and a measurement of how far it depends on the way the model is chosen. We curated inhibition constant (Ki) data for 33 human protein ta
papers.summary: The authors curated inhibition constant (Ki) data for 33 human protein targets to build a target-specific benchmark for potency prediction on activity-cliff compounds—pairs of structurally similar molecules with unexpectedly large potency differences. They quantify, per target, how poorly models predict these cliff compounds and how much the gap depends on model selection. This provides a standardized, single-endpoint panel for diagnosing where ligand-based potency prediction fails.

papers.title: A Comparison of Convolutional, Transformer, and State-Space U-Shaped Pipelines for Neuronal Soma Instance Segmentation in Label-Free 3D Microscopy.
papers.abstract: Instance segmentation of neuronal somata in label-free three-dimensional (3D) microscopy is challenging because of low contrast, crowding, and species- and modality-dependent appearance. We compared seven U-shaped semantic-to-instance pipelines (3D U-Net, nnU-Net v2, SwinUNETR, 3D TransUNet, U-Mamba, Swin-UMamba-3D, and an exploratory MedMamba-UNet) on 240 public volumes of six rat, mouse, and human species-modality subsets, using the released partition. Models were trained for 25,000 steps with three seeds, post-processing was selected on source-domain validation volumes, and native-grid pred
papers.summary: This study benchmarks seven U-shaped deep learning pipelines—spanning convolutional (3D U-Net, nnU-Net v2), transformer (SwinUNETR, 3D TransUNet), and state-space (U-Mamba, Swin-UMamba-3D, MedMamba-UNet) architectures—for instance segmentation of neuronal somata in label-free 3D microscopy across 240 volumes from rat, mouse, and human samples. Models were trained under a controlled protocol with multiple seeds and source-domain validation, providing a systematic comparison of architecture families for this challenging low-contrast, crowded segmentation task. The work offers practical guidance on which pipeline families perform best for label-free neuronal soma instance segmentation.

papers.title: Hybrid BiLSTM-Graph Neural Networks Learn Efficient Secondary Structure Representations for Protein-Protein Interface Prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-protein interfaces (PPIs) are essential for numerous biological processes and represent attractive targets for drug discovery and protein engineering. Although recent protein language models have enabled powerful sequence representations for downstream structural prediction tasks, they require substantial computational resources and produce general-purpose embeddings that are not optimized for specific applications. In this work, we investigate whether task-specific representation learning can provide a computationally efficient alternative for PPI prediction. Proteins are represented
papers.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid BiLSTM-graph neural network that learns task-specific secondary structure representations for predicting protein-protein interfaces, offering a lighter-weight alternative to large protein language models. The approach aims to capture structural information relevant to interface prediction without the computational cost of general-purpose embeddings. It demonstrates that specialized representation learning can be competitive for this focused task.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Enabled Multi-Sensor Framework for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis and Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Machinery.
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multi-sensor framework for condition monitoring and intelligent fault diagnosis in rotating industrial machinery, integrating heterogeneous sensing, machine-learning-based diagnosis, MQTT communication, historical data management, and a synchronized 3D Digital Twin. The experimental platform employs feature-level fusion by combining statistical and spectral descriptors extracted from vibration and acoustic signals with temporally aligned temperature and rotational-speed measurements to classify four machine-health states: Healthy, Minor, Moderate, and Severe. To assess th
papers.summary: The paper presents a multi-sensor condition-monitoring framework for rotating industrial machinery that fuses vibration, acoustic, temperature, and rotational-speed data with a synchronized 3D Digital Twin. Machine-learning classification distinguishes four health states (Healthy, Minor, Moderate, Severe), with MQTT-based communication and historical data management supporting predictive maintenance. The work is an engineering integration demonstration rather than a biological or bioinformatics contribution.

papers.title: Genomic Prediction for Powdery Mildew Resistance in Wheat: A Thirty-Model Benchmark of Conventional, Machine-Learning, and Deep-Learning Approaches.
papers.abstract: Powdery mildew, caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici (Bgt), is a major foliar disease of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.). Genomic prediction (GP) can accelerate breeding for this trait, but conventional, machine-learning (ML), and deep-learning (DL) methods have rarely been compared side by side. Using the Wheat Association Mapping Initiative (WAMI) panel (n = 286), phenotyped for powdery mildew severity over three years (DS1-DS3) and genotyped with the Illumina 90K SNP array, we compared 30 GP models under per-year and genotype-grouped pooled cross-validation. Broad-sense heritabilit
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 30 genomic prediction models—spanning conventional statistical approaches, machine learning, and deep learning—for powdery mildew resistance in a 286-line wheat panel genotyped with a 90K SNP array and phenotyped across three years. It provides a systematic side-by-side comparison of model families under both per-year and genotype-grouped cross-validation, addressing a gap in the literature where such methods are rarely evaluated together. The work offers practical guidance for breeders on which model types perform best for this disease trait.

papers.title: Accelerating MAPK1 Inhibitor Discovery Through Stacking Ensemble Learning with Graph Neural Networks.
papers.abstract: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1) plays a central role in cancer cell proliferation and survival. In this study, we developed an ensemble graph neural network framework integrating graph convolutional neural networks, graph message-passing neural networks, and attention-based graph neural networks to predict MAPK1 inhibitory activity using large-scale quantitative high-throughput screening data. Our models achieved recall ranging from 79.5% to 92.3%, areas under the precision-recall curve ranging from 80.4% to 90.3%, and Matthews correlation coefficients ranging from 0.523 to 0.725 on
papers.summary: The authors built a stacking ensemble of three graph neural network architectures (GCN, MPNN, and attention-based GNN) to predict whether compounds inhibit MAPK1, a kinase central to cancer cell proliferation. Trained on large-scale quantitative high-throughput screening data, the ensemble achieved strong recall (79.5–92.3%), AUPRC (80.4–90.3%), and MCC (0.523–0.725), suggesting it can effectively prioritize candidate MAPK1 inhibitors.

papers.title: Multi-Omics and Explainable Artificial Intelligence Reveal Peimine Modulates Macrophage Polarization Homeostasis via CCR3/ITK/S1PR5/PRKCQ and MMP8/UGCG/KLF5 Axes in Pneumonia.
papers.abstract: Pneumonia is driven by disordered immune inflammation dominated by dysregulated macrophage polarization. Peimine, the major bioactive steroidal alkaloid of Fritillariae Bulbus, exerts anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, whereas its direct targets and the metabolic routes through which it may influence macrophage polarization in pneumonia remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics data with explainable AI to identify how the natural compound peimine influences macrophage polarization in pneumonia. The authors propose that peimine acts through two molecular axes—CCR3/ITK/S1PR5/PRKCQ and MMP8/UGCG/KLF5—to restore balance between pro- and anti-inflammatory macrophage states. The work nominates candidate targets and metabolic pathways for peimine's immunomodulatory effects, though experimental validation appears limited.

papers.title: StrongGeneAgent: An Evidence-Grounded Conversational Agent for Gene-Centric Pan-Cancer Multi-Omics Analysis.
papers.abstract: Single-gene analysis remains a common entry point for investigating cancer biology, yet integrating evidence for a target gene across molecular layers, tumor types, and clinical endpoints remains fragmented across specialized tools and workflows. Here, we present StrongGeneAgent, an evidence-grounded conversational framework for natural-language, gene-centric multi-omics analysis across cancer types.
papers.summary: StrongGeneAgent is a conversational agent that lets researchers query a single gene across multiple molecular layers, tumor types, and clinical endpoints using natural language. It grounds its answers in evidence from pan-cancer multi-omics data, aiming to replace fragmented tool-by-tool workflows with a unified, chat-based interface. The work is presented as a framework rather than a validated benchmarked system.

papers.title: Biologically Inspired Selective Attention for Prostate MRI: A Segmentation-Guided Vision Transformer Framework for Computer-Aided Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men, yet interpretation of multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) suffers from substantial inter-observer variability and depends on scarce expert radiologists. Expert readers follow a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine visual strategy: they first localize the prostate gland and then direct focused attention to tissue within it. Inspired by this biological selective-attention mechanism, we propose a segmentation-guided framework in which a modality-aware 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) first delineates the prostate gland from T2-weighted, ADC, and
papers.summary: The authors propose a segmentation-guided 3D Vision Transformer for prostate cancer diagnosis on multiparametric MRI, inspired by how expert radiologists first localize the prostate gland and then focus attention on tissue within it. The model uses a modality-aware ViT to delineate the gland from T2-weighted and ADC images, then directs diagnostic attention to the segmented region. This biologically inspired coarse-to-fine design aims to reduce inter-observer variability and reliance on scarce expert radiologists.

papers.title: Systemic Inflammatory Markers and Quantitative Stool Culture in Machine Learning Classification of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: An Exploratory Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) studies of the gut microbiota rarely test whether microbial data add anything to routine clinical and inflammatory markers. We examined this question in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) using quantitative stool culture. In this exploratory case-control study, 52 adults with IBD and 34 hospital controls underwent clinical, anthropometric, bioimpedance, biochemical and inflammatory assessment, together with quantitative stool culture interpreted against laboratory reference intervals. Six classifiers were evaluated with repeated nested cross-validation (5 folds × 10 repeats
papers.summary: This exploratory case-control study tested whether quantitative stool culture data improve machine learning classification of inflammatory bowel disease beyond routine clinical and inflammatory markers. Using six classifiers with repeated nested cross-validation in 52 IBD patients and 34 controls, the work directly addresses whether microbial data add incremental predictive value over standard clinical variables.

papers.title: Explainable Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Differential Diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis and Neuromyelitis Optica Using 3D MRI Lesion Features.
papers.abstract: Neurological disorders are among the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide, making timely and accurate diagnosis essential. Differential diagnosis (DD) of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) and Neuromyelitis Optica (NMO) spectrum disorder using brain MRI remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and similar lesion characteristics. To address this challenge, this study proposes a neuroinformatics-driven computer-aided differential diagnosis (CADD) framework that automatically extracts, encodes, and analyzes quantitative 3D lesion biomarkers from brain MRI using deep lea
papers.summary: The authors propose a computer-aided differential diagnosis framework that automatically extracts and encodes quantitative 3D lesion biomarkers from brain MRI using deep learning to distinguish Multiple Sclerosis from Neuromyelitis Optica spectrum disorder. The approach aims to address the clinical challenge of overlapping lesion characteristics and clinical presentations between these two demyelinating diseases, with explainability built into the model.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a ligand-aware benchmark for predicting protein-ligand binding sites at residue resolution, evaluating models across three regimes: ligands with abundant training data, underrepresented ligands, and completely unseen (zero-shot) ligands. The framework uses a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering to systematically assess how predictive performance varies with data availability. It provides a structured evaluation approach for zero-shot binding-site prediction from protein sequence and SMILES representations.

papers.title: Protify: A Benchmarking Platform Revealing Task Dependence and Homology Leakage in Protein Language Model Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Protein Language Models (pLMs) have become essential tools for computational protein analysis, and the rapid proliferation of architectures, training objectives, and pretraining corpora has produced a diverse and expanding model landscape. Evaluation practices, however, remain fragmented: studies use different datasets, preprocessing pipelines, and reporting conventions, so results rarely transfer between publications. Here we introduce Protify, an open-source platform that standardizes pLM benchmarking across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings through a unified, low-code in
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Protify is an open-source platform that standardizes benchmarking of protein language models across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings using a unified, low-code interface. The work reveals that evaluation outcomes are strongly task-dependent and that homology leakage between pretraining and evaluation data can inflate performance, highlighting the need for standardized, leakage-aware benchmarking.

papers.title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ∼15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PALM, a protein language model that combines ESM2 embeddings with LoRA fine-tuning, learned layer aggregation, and a BiLSTM to jointly predict protein domains and functional sites, while allowing overlapping and nested annotations via a soft-target objective. Trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences, PALM aims to help annotate the growing backlog of uncharacterized proteins and coding variants. The work extends protein language models toward multi-label functional annotation and variant effect prediction.

papers.title: RepurposeAD: Knowledge Graph-Guided LLM Reasoning for Alzheimer's Drug Repurposing.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Alzheimer's disease (AD) drug development continues to suffer from high late-stage attrition and narrow mechanistic diversity, which makes the systematic repurposing of approved compounds an urgent priority. Existing computational repurposing methods operate on fragmented biomedical knowledge, rarely integrate transcriptomic and pharmacological evidence within a single reasoning process, and provide little of the mechanistic transparency required for clinical translation. This paper presents RepurposeAD, a knowledge graph-guided large language model (LLM) reasoning frame
papers.summary: RepurposeAD is a framework that combines knowledge graphs with large language model reasoning to identify existing approved drugs that could be repurposed for Alzheimer's disease. It integrates transcriptomic and pharmacological evidence within a single reasoning pipeline, aiming to improve mechanistic transparency compared to prior computational repurposing approaches. The work targets the high attrition rate and narrow mechanistic diversity in AD drug development.

papers.title: CASP1 and SPTAN1 Identified as Potential PANoptosis-Related Biomarkers for Differentiating Active Tuberculosis from Latent Tuberculosis Infection Through Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis and Exploratory In Vitro Assessment.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing active tuberculosis (ATB) from latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) remains a critical unmet need in tuberculosis control. PANoptosis, a newly recognized form of programmed cell death (PCD) integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, may provide novel biomarkers for this distinction. To explore this, transcriptomic datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were employed to identify PANoptosis-related differentially expressed genes (TPAN_DEGs) between ATB and LTBI. An ensemble machine-learning approach combining least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), S
papers.summary: This study used integrative bioinformatics on public transcriptomic datasets to identify PANoptosis-related genes that distinguish active tuberculosis from latent infection, narrowing candidates via ensemble machine learning (LASSO and related methods). CASP1 and SPTAN1 emerged as potential biomarkers, with exploratory in vitro validation. The work proposes a novel biomarker panel but remains preliminary and requires larger clinical validation.

papers.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
papers.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: VIGAT is a new tool that uses a vision-language model to automatically interpret ATAC-seq coverage plots and adaptively quantify gene activity from single-cell ATAC-seq data. By jointly examining accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes and integrating genomic annotations, it selects gene-specific regions that are more informative for distinguishing cell types than broadly accessible regions. This addresses a key challenge in scATAC-seq analysis where informative regulatory regions vary across genes and tissues.

papers.title: Outcomes Reported in Randomised Controlled Trials of Pharmacological Treatments for Acute Viral Respiratory Infections in Hospitalised Adults: A Rapid Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of pharmacological treatments for acute viral respiratory infections (AVRIs) report outcomes that vary in selection, definition, timing, and measurement, thereby hampering evidence synthesis and comparability across clinical trials. This rapid scoping review mapped the outcomes, definitions, time points, and measurement instruments reported in RCTs of pharmacological treatments for hospitalised adults with AVRIs. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from June 2015 to June 2025 for RCTs, including adaptive and platform trials, that enroled hospitalised ad
papers.summary: This rapid scoping review maps the outcomes, definitions, timing, and measurement instruments used in randomised controlled trials of pharmacological treatments for acute viral respiratory infections in hospitalised adults. The authors find substantial heterogeneity across trials, which hampers evidence synthesis and cross-trial comparability. The work highlights the need for standardised outcome sets in this clinical area.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for estimation of volume and surface optical parameters in skin hyperspectral imaging using one- and two-layer tissue models.
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is a non-invasive optical modality capable of characterizing biological tissues, making it suitable for medical applications such as skin lesion analysis. However, recovering physiological and optical tissue parameters from hyperspectral skin data remains a challenging inverse problem due to the high dimensionality and complexity of light-tissue interactions. We hypothesize that physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can separate surface and volume reflections while recovering optical properties directly from hyperspectral skin images. To test this hypothesis, fou
papers.summary: This paper applies physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to the inverse problem of recovering optical absorption and scattering parameters from hyperspectral skin images, using both one-layer and two-layer tissue models. The authors hypothesize that PINNs can disentangle surface from volume reflections while estimating tissue optical properties directly from the data. The work is a methodological contribution to non-invasive skin imaging, with potential relevance to skin lesion analysis.

papers.title: Morus Prenylflavonoids as Candidate NLRP3 Inflammasome Inhibitors from an AI-Guided Natural-Product Screen with a Quantified Applicability Domain.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The NLRP3 (NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 3) inflammasome drives interleukin-1β maturation and pyroptosis in chronic inflammatory disease, and no direct inhibitor has been approved. Natural products are a plausible source of new chemical matter for this target, but such collections are too large to dock exhaustively, and the machine-learning rankings used to triage them are routinely acted on without stating the chemistry over which they hold. This study prioritises natural-product candidates for NLRP3 while quantifying that limit explicitly. Methods: In t
papers.summary: This study uses an AI-guided virtual screening approach to prioritize natural-product prenylflavonoids from Morus (mulberry) as candidate NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors, a target lacking any approved direct inhibitor. A notable methodological feature is that the authors explicitly quantify the applicability domain of their machine-learning model, addressing a common weakness in AI-based triage where rankings are used without stating the chemical space over which they are valid.

papers.title: ADCCR: Adaptive Description Composition and Coarse-to-Fine Refinement for Language-Guided Human Keypoint Localization.
papers.abstract: Biological vision integrates cues according to their reliability and context and uses coarse contextual information to form initial hypotheses before directing attention to local evidence. Inspired by these principles, we propose ADCCR (Adaptive Description Composition and Coarse-to-Fine Refinement), a language-guided framework for flexible human keypoint localization. A multi-granularity bank describes each keypoint by its name, anatomical definition, inter-joint relation, and visual appearance. A reliability-aware composer predicts sample-specific gates from the person image, target identity
papers.summary: ADCCR is a language-guided framework for localizing human keypoints (joints) in images, inspired by how biological vision combines cues by reliability and refines from coarse to fine. It uses a multi-granularity description bank (keypoint name, anatomical definition, inter-joint relations, visual appearance) and a reliability-aware composer that predicts sample-specific weights, followed by coarse-to-fine refinement. The work is a computer-vision method with biomimetic inspiration rather than a biological or omics contribution.

papers.title: Lineage-aware evaluation of machine learning for observed cross-genus occurrence of IncC plasmids in public databases.
papers.abstract: IncC plasmids contribute to the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance across bacterial hosts. We developed an IncC-specific model to classify plasmids belonging to highly similar cross-genus pairs observed in public databases and evaluated its performance when related lineages were kept together during validation.
papers.summary: The authors built a machine-learning classifier to distinguish IncC plasmids from other plasmids, focusing on highly similar plasmid pairs found across different bacterial genera in public databases. They show that standard validation can overestimate performance when closely related lineages are split between training and test sets, and that lineage-aware validation gives a more realistic picture of how well the model generalizes to new hosts.

papers.title: Cross-channel temporal fusion for retail customer lifetime value prediction: architecture, ablation, and causal validation of a gated BiGRU fusion network.
papers.abstract: Predicting customer lifetime value (CLV) in non-contractual retail settings is complicated by purchase sequence sparsity and heterogeneous engagement across marketing channels.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a gated bidirectional GRU fusion network that combines purchase sequences with cross-channel engagement data to predict customer lifetime value in non-contractual retail settings. The authors report architecture details, ablation studies, and causal validation, showing that fusing temporal signals across channels improves CLV prediction over single-channel baselines.

papers.title: Discrimination between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and hypertensive heart disease using deep learning-based magnetic resonance imaging.
papers.abstract: Discrimination between HCM and HHD can be challenging due to overlapping imaging presentation and clinical features. This study aimed to develop a deep learning pipeline for discrimination between hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and hypertensive heart disease (HHD) using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images.
papers.summary: This study develops a deep learning pipeline applied to cardiovascular magnetic resonance images to distinguish hypertrophic cardiomyopathy from hypertensive heart disease, two conditions with overlapping imaging and clinical features. The work aims to improve diagnostic discrimination in a clinically challenging differential diagnosis.

papers.title: Clinical effectiveness of Biqi capsule combined with methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis: an integrated retrospective, meta-analytic, and machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) monotherapy provides inadequate disease control in many patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Biqi Capsule (BQC), a proprietary traditional Chinese medicine formulation, is used as an adjunct to MTX, but its clinical benefits remain uncertain.
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether adding Biqi Capsule, a traditional Chinese medicine formulation, to methotrexate improves outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis patients. It combines a retrospective clinical analysis, a meta-analysis of prior trials, and machine learning to identify which patients benefit most. The findings suggest BQC plus MTX may offer clinical advantages over MTX alone, though the evidence base is heterogeneous.

papers.title: Anesthesia-associated pro-inflammatory microglial transcriptional signatures: transcriptomic identification and multi-dataset characterization of five candidate hub genes.
papers.abstract: To identify candidate hub genes associated with anesthesia-related microglial pro-inflammatory transcriptional changes and to explore their computationally inferred upstream transcriptional regulators, providing candidate molecular correlates that require future clinical validation before any relevance to perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) can be inferred.
papers.summary: This study analyzes transcriptomic datasets to identify five candidate hub genes linked to pro-inflammatory microglial activation after anesthesia, along with computationally predicted upstream transcriptional regulators. The findings are exploratory and explicitly require future clinical validation before any connection to perioperative neurocognitive disorder can be drawn.

papers.title: Survival of the fittest tool: choosing between open and closed artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical science.
papers.abstract: Three years ago, this journal published the editorial Technological Darwinism, urging pharmaceutical scientists to adapt to artificial intelligence (AI) rather than resist it. Since then, the question has shifted from whether to use AI to which AI to use, under what circumstances, and with what evidence. This review addresses that question by mapping current AI tools across the five canonical stages of drug development, from discovery to post-market pharmacovigilance. It is a narrative review, not a systematic one, and it treats openness as a spectrum rather than a binary. It compares two broa
papers.journal: Journal of pharmacy & pharmaceutical sciences : a publication of the Canadian Society for Pharmaceutical Sciences, Societe canadienne des sciences pharmaceutiques
papers.summary: This narrative review maps current AI tools across the five canonical stages of drug development, from discovery through post-market pharmacovigilance, and compares open versus closed AI approaches. It argues that openness should be treated as a spectrum rather than a binary and frames the central question as which AI to use, under what circumstances, and with what evidence. The paper offers guidance for pharmaceutical scientists navigating tool selection rather than a systematic evaluation of performance.

papers.title: Selective representation learning boosts intrinsically disordered protein prediction from pretrained language models.
papers.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins and intrinsically disordered regions lack stable tertiary structures yet play indispensable roles in cellular signaling, regulation, and disease processes. Predicting disorder from sequence alone remains a fundamental challenge in computational biology. Recent advances in pretrained protein language models have shown great potential in capturing rich contextual representations. However, hierarchical pretrained protein language model features suffer from token-level noise and multi-layer redundancy, which limits their efficacy in downstream tasks.
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of predicting intrinsically disordered proteins and regions from sequence by improving how features are extracted from pretrained protein language models. The authors propose a selective representation learning approach to reduce token-level noise and multi-layer redundancy in hierarchical language model features, which they show boosts downstream disorder prediction performance.

papers.title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
papers.abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. We define the Predictive Dermatome as a computationally derived, anatomically localized skin region characterized by a shared or probabilistically related biological aging state and trajectory inferred from integrated molecular, structural, imaging, cl
papers.summary: This paper proposes a conceptual framework called the 'Predictive Dermatome,' which defines computationally derived, anatomically localized skin regions that share a biological aging state and trajectory. The authors argue that chronological age and systemic aging clocks cannot capture the spatial heterogeneity of skin aging, and they outline how integrated molecular, structural, imaging, and clinical data could be used with spatial AI to map region-specific aging. The work is a technical framework rather than an empirical study.

papers.title: ToxiFusion: integrating contextual and compositional sequence representations for toxic peptide prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting of toxic peptides from sequence information is important for peptide safety assessment and therapeutic development. However, reported performance of computational predictors can be affected by representation limitations and evaluation bias.
papers.summary: ToxiFusion introduces a computational method for predicting toxic peptides directly from their amino acid sequences by combining contextual and compositional sequence representations. The work addresses representation limitations and evaluation bias that can affect existing predictors, aiming to improve the reliability of peptide safety assessment for therapeutic development.
